questions: Is your main concern involuntary movement or shaking of your arms or hands?
Does it affect one side of your body more than the other?
Do you remain fully aware during the episodes?
Can you stop the movement if you consciously try?
Does it become worse when someone watches or examines you?
Is it triggered by stress, fear, or emotional upset?
Have you had any new weakness?
Have you had numbness or loss of sensation?
Have you had trouble speaking, seeing, walking, or maintaining balance?
Have you lost consciousness or had a seizure?
Have you had chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath?
Did the symptoms follow a recent injury, illness, or infection?
Have you started or changed any medication recently?
Have you used alcohol, recreational drugs, or stimulants shortly before the symptoms began?
Have you had similar episodes in the past?
Do you have a history of neurological or psychiatric illness?

DIAGNOSIS: Sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (prion-associated rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease), presenting with unilateral cortical myoclonus/tremor

Autoimmune encephalitis, particularly anti-LGI1 or anti-NMDA-receptor encephalitis
